prompt: A colleague starts every meeting with a funny story and knows everyone's weekend plans.
tells: starts every meeting with a funny story
why: Social, warm and talkative is i.
trap: S is warm too, but quieter and less the center of attention.

prompt: In brainstorms, one teammate throws out twenty ideas in ten minutes, many half-formed and all exciting to him.
trap: D wants to pick one and act, not generate twenty.

prompt: She sells the client on a great vision but forgets to send the contract and mixes up the dates.
why: Big-picture enthusiasm with weak follow-through on detail is i.
trap: D also skips detail, but rarely drops the result itself.

prompt: Before deciding, he needs to talk the idea through with three people and changes his mind twice while talking.
tells: talk the idea through with three people
why: i processes ideas out loud, socially.
trap: S also seeks others' views, but to make sure everyone is comfortable, and decides slowly.

prompt: A teammate glows when his manager praises him in front of the whole department.
tells: in front of the whole department
why: i is motivated by public recognition.
trap: S often prefers private thanks and can feel awkward in the spotlight.

prompt: After a cool reaction to her pitch, an upbeat colleague spends the afternoon worried that people don't like her.
tells: worried that people don't like her
why: i's biggest fear is rejection or loss of approval.
trap: S worries about conflict, but about the relationship's stability rather than being liked.

prompt: His messages are full of exclamation marks and emojis: 'Love this!!! Let's grab coffee and riff on it 🎉'
tells: full of exclamation marks and emojis
trap: D writes short; i writes warm.

prompt: Under stress, a normally cheerful teammate gets scattered, overpromises and talks over others.
why: Under stress, i becomes disorganized and overly talkative.
trap: D under stress gets controlling, not scattered.

prompt: Whenever the team needs buy-in from another department, everyone sends Jamie, who can get anyone excited.
why: Persuading and energizing others is i's strength.
trap: D can push decisions through; i gets people to want them.

prompt: His estimates are always optimistic: 'Easy, we'll have it done by Friday!' It's rarely done by Friday.
tells: 'Easy, we'll have it done by Friday!'
why: Optimism that underestimates the work is i.
trap: D might push a short deadline, but as a demand, not cheerful optimism.
